memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses: 'Set up the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, on the first day of the first month.'" - Exod 40:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Everything was built. The materials were counted, the garments woven, the work inspected and blessed. And still Israel waited for God to say when.

He named a date: the first day of the first month. Almost exactly one year after they left Egypt.

There is something worth learning in that. Readiness is not the same as permission. The tabernacle could have been assembled the day the last peg was made, but God's people waited for God's word.

We are usually the opposite. Once we are able to do something, we assume we should. Ability feels like authorisation. But wisdom often lies in the gap between "I could" and "God has said."

Notice the timing God chose. The first day of the first month — a fresh beginning, a new year, a clean start. God is deliberate about when He does things. He is never late and rarely early by our reckoning.

Paul says that at just the right time, when we were still powerless, Christ died for the ungodly (Rom 5:6). And when the set time had fully come, God sent His Son (Gal 4:4).

If you are waiting on something God has clearly promised, the waiting is not wasted. He has a date.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you rushing ahead of God because you feel ready?
2. What are you waiting for, and can you trust His timing with it?
3. Where do you need to hear that God has a date even when you cannot see it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me wait for Your word rather than acting simply because I am able. Your timing is good. Amen.
